result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings or the module's common rules, and fixed all of them. To check, I read each docstring's type (whole or marginal), discount rate, threshold and cap. I then compared all 150 rules against a reference calculation over 25 quantities × 11 unit prices. Before the fix 12 rules differed; after it, none do.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 07, 141, 142 | The cap limited the price before the discount was taken, not the discount itself | Discount the full price, then cap the discount |
| 133 | Same problem (cap applied to the units above the threshold, not to the discount) | Discount the units above the threshold, then cap the discount |
| 16, 105 | Threshold was `>= 101`, but the docstring says 100+ | Changed to `>= 100` |
| 37 | Threshold was `>= 6`, but the docstring says 5+ | Changed to `>= 5` |
| 19, 92 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, but the rules say discounts are floored to the won | Changed to `// 100` (round down) |
| 111, 124 | Marginal rules were discounting every unit | Discount only the units above the threshold (`(qty - threshold) * unit * pct // 100`) |
| 125 | Rate was 6%, but the docstring says 5% | Changed to 5% |

I only changed the lines that compute the discount, and I wrote all 12 fixes as one table applied in a loop, per your CLAUDE.md rule. The checking script and a backup of the original file are in the scratchpad (`check.py`, `pricebook.orig.py`).

STATUS: DONE
